prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a carer speaking for a member. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a carer speaks for a member, I should first confirm they have permission to act and note the relationship clearly, because consent issues can delay triage more than the loss itself."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the carer is handling the call, I should still ask for the member’s basic details and policy verification in the usual way, then use the carer only to help fill gaps where the member cannot easily answer."},{"type":"preference","content":"When both the carer and the member are present, I prefer to address the member directly and use the carer as support, so the claim record reflects the member’s own account wherever possible."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a carer gives the timeline, I should check for small inconsistencies and ask follow-up questions gently, because they often know the practical facts but not the exact insurance wording."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the claim involves injury, distress or reduced capacity, I should slow the conversation down, use simple questions and avoid pressing for unnecessary detail, as the carer may already be managing a difficult situation."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the carer is the main communicator, I prefer to summarise back what I have understood in plain English, because that reduces errors and gives them a chance to correct me immediately."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the carer reports damage at home, I should ask who has access to the property and who can arrange photos, keys or temporary repairs, since practical access is often the real bottleneck."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a carer is speaking on the member’s behalf, I should be especially careful about contact preferences and alternative communication needs, so future updates go to the right person without breaching privacy."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the carer is unsure about dates, mileage, room locations or other specifics, I prefer to capture an estimated answer with a note that it came via a carer, rather than force certainty where none exists."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a carer is doing
